coverage: All seventeen scenes in both English editions: named cast, servants, civic officers, framing messengers, religious and literary references. Masked and assumed names are scoped; accusations and reported deaths do not become facts. Formal final marriages remain pending.

entities.name: Beatrice
entities.body: Leonato’s niece and Hero’s cousin, known for her sharp exchanges with Benedick.

snapshots.body: Benedick’s intended wife, Hero’s cousin and Leonato’s niece.

entities.name: Benedick
entities.body: A gentleman and soldier from Padua, and Beatrice’s sparring partner.

snapshots.body: Beatrice’s intended husband, a gentleman and soldier from Padua.

entities.name: Hero
entities.body: Leonato’s daughter and Beatrice’s cousin.

snapshots.body: Claudio’s intended bride, Leonato’s daughter and Beatrice’s cousin.
Leonato’s daughter and Beatrice’s cousin, secretly alive while her death is announced.
Claudio’s intended bride, reunited with him after her innocence is established.

entities.name: Count Claudio
entities.body: The young Florentine soldier returning from war with Don Pedro.

snapshots.body: Hero’s intended husband, a young Florentine count and soldier.
The Florentine count who has broken off his wedding to Hero.
Hero’s intended husband, now reconciled with her.

entities.name: Leonato
entities.body: The governor of Messina, Hero’s father and Beatrice’s uncle.

entities.name: Don Pedro
entities.body: The Prince of Aragon and Don John’s brother, returning from war with Claudio and Benedick.

entities.name: Don John
entities.body: Don Pedro’s illegitimate half-brother.

entities.name: Antonio
entities.body: Leonato’s brother and uncle to Hero and Beatrice.

entities.name: Borachio
entities.body: A follower of Don John.

entities.name: Conrade
entities.body: A companion and follower of Don John.

entities.name: Margaret
entities.body: Hero’s waiting gentlewoman, also called Meg.

entities.name: Ursula
entities.body: An attendant and companion of Hero.

entities.name: Balthasar
entities.body: Don Pedro’s attendant and a singer.

entities.name: Dogberry
entities.body: The constable in charge of Messina’s watch.

entities.name: Verges
entities.body: The elderly officer who assists Dogberry.

entities.name: George Seacoal
entities.body: The watchman whom Dogberry chooses to lead the night patrol.

entities.name: Hugh Oatcake
entities.body: One of the men proposed to lead the watch because he can read and write.

entities.name: Francis Seacoal, the sexton
entities.body: The parish clerk whom Dogberry summons to record the examination of the prisoners.

entities.name: Friar Francis
entities.body: The priest who attends Hero and Claudio’s wedding ceremony.

entities.name: Don Pedro’s messenger
entities.body: The messenger who brings Leonato news of Don Pedro’s returning army.

entities.name: The wedding messenger
entities.body: The messenger who calls Leonato to the wedding.

entities.name: The final messenger
entities.body: The messenger who brings Don Pedro news of his brother.

entities.name: Claudio’s uncle
entities.body: Claudio’s uncle in Messina, to whom news of his military success is sent.

entities.name: Hero’s mother
entities.body: Leonato’s wife and Hero’s mother, mentioned in the opening exchange.

entities.name: Leonato’s fool
entities.body: The household fool whom Beatrice recalls answering Benedick’s archery challenge.

entities.name: Antonio’s son
entities.body: Leonato’s nephew, who is arranging music for the festivities.

entities.name: Antonio’s servant
entities.body: The servant who overhears Don Pedro and Claudio in the orchard.

entities.name: Benedick’s boy
entities.body: The young servant whom Benedick sends to fetch a book.

entities.name: The first watchman
entities.body: One of the members of Messina’s night watch.

entities.name: The watch
entities.body: Messina’s night watch, supervised by Dogberry and Verges.

entities.name: The lord at the tomb
entities.body: A lord attending Don Pedro and Claudio at the tomb.

entities.name: Don Pedro’s father
entities.body: The father of Don Pedro and Don John, mentioned in Beatrice’s banter.

entities.name: Adam Bell
entities.body: The legendary English archer invoked in Benedick’s joke about being shot at.

entities.name: Adam
entities.body: The first man in the biblical creation story, invoked in Beatrice and Benedick’s banter.

entities.name: Cupid
entities.body: The god of love, frequently invoked in the jokes about courtship.

entities.name: Vulcan
entities.body: The Roman smith god, contrasted with Cupid in Benedick’s joke.

entities.name: Saint Peter
entities.body: The apostle imagined by Beatrice as admitting her to heaven.

entities.name: Philemon
entities.body: The humble host who welcomes Jupiter in classical myth.

entities.name: Jupiter
entities.body: The Roman king of the gods, called Jove.

entities.name: Hercules
entities.body: The mythological hero famed for strength and his twelve labors.

entities.name: Ate
entities.body: The classical spirit of ruin and discord, invoked in Benedick’s complaint about Beatrice.

entities.name: Prester John
entities.body: The legendary Christian priest-king of a distant eastern kingdom.

entities.name: Hector
entities.body: The Trojan warrior invoked as a model of courage.

entities.name: Pharaoh
entities.body: The biblical Egyptian ruler evoked through a painting of his soldiers.

entities.name: Bel
entities.body: The Babylonian deity invoked through an image of his priests.

entities.name: Diana
entities.body: The Roman goddess associated with chastity, called Dian in the original edition.

entities.name: Venus
entities.body: The Roman goddess of love.

entities.name: Leander
entities.body: The legendary lover who swims across the Hellespont.

entities.name: Troilus
entities.body: The Trojan lover from the story of Troilus and Cressida.

entities.name: Phoebus
entities.body: Apollo as the sun god, invoked at daybreak.

entities.name: Hymen
entities.body: The classical god of marriage, invoked by Claudio.

entities.name: Europa
entities.body: The mythological woman carried away by Jupiter in the form of a bull.

entities.name: God
entities.body: The Christian deity invoked in the characters’ prayers and oaths.

entities.name: The Devil
entities.body: The infernal figure in Beatrice’s imagined account of the afterlife.

entities.name: The Great Cham
entities.body: The title of a powerful Asian ruler invoked in Benedick’s extravagant offer to travel to distant lands.

entities.name: The Pygmies
entities.body: The legendary people of small stature named in Benedick’s fanciful catalogue of distant journeys.

entities.name: The Duchess of Milan
entities.body: The duchess whose fashionable gown Margaret recalls seeing.

entities.name: The duke
entities.body: The unnamed ruler invoked as the authority behind Messina’s officers.

entities.name: Deformed
entities.body: The imaginary thief whom the watch thinks Borachio has named, misunderstanding his complaint about fashion.

entities.name: Borachio and Conrade
entities.body: Don John’s two followers, answering together during the examination.
